title: Systemically Important Banks and Loan Performance: Evidence from India
eligible_reason: Staggered DiD with a binary absorbing treatment: sib_ind = 1 for loans of a bank from the year it is designated a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (SBI and ICICI in 2016, HDFC in 2018), 0 otherwise; two distinct adoption years, 43 never-treated banks, bank-firm-year panel 2010-2020. Table 4 column 1 is a linear regression of new_default on sib_ind with bank-firm pair FE (creditorcode##firmcode, the unit) and firm-by-year FE (firmcode##year, a time-invariant unit characteristic interacted with calendar time), no controls, clustered by bank. Table 8 column 1 is a bank-year TWFE (creditorcode and year FE) of the NPA write-off ratio on sib_ind with no controls. Figure 2 reports Sun-Abraham interaction-weighted estimates (eventstudyinteract) of the same design with never-treated banks as controls, which the protocol admits. Columns adding bank-year or loan controls (Table 4 columns 2-3, Figure 1 event study, Table 8 column 2) and the exposure-based firm-level tables (Tables 5-7) are not eligible.
design_notes: Intermediate dta/MCA_Default_Yearly v2.dta: bank x firm x year panel built from MCA charge registrations with loans >= Rs 10 million, foreign banks dropped, 2009-2020 (2020 Q3-Q4 dropped); analysis sample 2010-2020 has 356,787 observations, 46 banks, 21,101 firms, 55,966 bank-firm pairs; new_default mean 0.0153; 11.7% of observations treated. Treated banks: creditorcode 236328 (SBI, 2016; 44,098 obs), 96379 (ICICI, 2016; 18,664 obs), 88297 (HDFC, 2018; 31,213 obs). Event-time indicators pre5-pre2, pre1 (zeroed, omitted), post0-post4 are in the data. Table 4 column 1 drops 122,178 singletons (firm-years with a single bank) leaving 234,609 observations and 46 clusters. Table 8 uses Raw dta/npa_w_off.dta merged to bank_list.dta (46 banks), 2010-2020, npa_woff = npa_w_off / npa, 423 bank-years, 45 clusters. Figure 1: event study with bank-year and loan controls (ineligible). Figure 2: eventstudyinteract with cohort(first_treat) in {2016, 2018}, control_cohort(never_treat), dynamic version with pre5-pre2 post0-post4; two aggregate SA ATT runs (never-treated control and last-cohort control) are also computed and may be reported in the text. Figure 3: bank placebo via R felm. Tables 5-7 use firm-year collapsed data with a lagged above-median DSIB exposure indicator (time-varying, non-absorbing) and conditional-on-default samples. Appendix: A5 double clustering of Table 4; A8-A9 subsamples; A7 Cox hazard; A12-A13 placebos.

data_files_note: Package ships raw and intermediate Stata files sufficient to run all tables; README does not describe the data as synthetic or disguised. Sources: MCA charge registry, CIBIL defaults, RBI, Prowess/CMIE.
software_notes: Stata 17 (reghdfe, eventstudyinteract, avar, event_plot, coefplot); R (lfe::felm) for the Figure 3 placebo.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Table numbering: README lists Table 3 as 'Bank-Firm Level Event Study' but code_main_tables.do produces Tables 1, 2, 4-8 and code_appendix_tables.do produces A2-A13, so Table 3 is probably the Figure 1 regression (with controls) in tabular form; check against the article. Only two adoption cohorts and three treated banks: eligible under the two-cohort rule but with heavy cluster concentration (treated banks account for 94,000 of 356,787 observations). Published coefficients above are taken from the authors' shipped log, not from the article PDF.
